Please go through all of our conversations, all of the data created, all of the artifacts, tests and synthesize what we learn for the challenge. Then, in one pruned new branch, only keep what is essential to share. minus all the bullshit, that came along the way. Is there anything unclear? Use ask_user, if unclear what i want.". Briefly acknowledge the goal, then immediately start (or continue) working toward it — treat the condition itself as your directive and do not pause to ask the user what to do. The hook will block stopping until the condition holds. It auto-clears once the condition is met — do not tell the user to run `/goal clear` after success; that's only for clearing a goal early.
Goal noted: survey every branch, conversation, data and artifact, synthesize the learnings, then build one pruned branch with only the essentials. Starting with a survey of the repo.

1	# Learnings
2	
3	Running list of what we found out about the arena, the suppliers and the data. Newest entry on
4	top of each section. How to add entries: `AGENTS.md`, "The learning loop".
5	
6	Tags: `arena` seen in a session (cite session or case), `data` from the data package (cite table
7	or ID), `rules` follows from `docs/api.md` or the kit's code. Untested ideas go under Hypotheses
8	until a session confirms or kills them.
9	
10	## Score and terms
11	
12	- 2026-10-10 `arena` **Coverage first.** P08 and P18 (raw material, 24-month need) closed at 12 months:
13	  uncovered need was half of C (P08 EUR 542k of 1,117k). C_best implies 4.27 vs our 5.93 (P08) and
14	  3.10 vs 6.00 (P18) at the same 12-month terms, i.e. the gap is coverage, not price. Both suppliers
15	  picked the 90-day sheet over the 24-month sheet and kept 12 months when we asked for both.
16	  → Lock contract length / volume to cover need x horizon before anything else. Probe: `notes/probe-results.md`.
17	- 2026-10-10 `arena` **Never send a sheet at or above the supplier's price.** P05: our anchor was
18	  floored at 97 % of should-cost (35.76), above Hrvelec's 31.50 quote; Hrvelec "agreed" at 35.76 and the
19	  case scored 0.01 (C_best implies 26.20). Code bug in the probe, but the rule holds for the agent.
20	- 2026-10-10 `arena` **Walking away still reveals `c_best`.** D01 walk-away after one message
21	  returned c_open 448,810.67, c_best 408,623.99, score 0 (sandbox). Every practice session gives the
22	  case's floor value however it ends, so a probe can spend all rounds on experiments.
23	- 2026-10-10 `arena` **Coverage beats price.** D01 (sandbox, kit's naive agent) scored 0.20. It
24	  talked the price from 52.90 to 50.90 but signed 12 months on a 24-month need, so EUR 231k of the
25	  EUR 441k C was uncovered need plus its risk. The same 50.90 with 24 months and a 2027-04-01 start
26	  scores 0.81 (relationship charge left out). Evidence: `logs/sessions/sandbox/D01_b3db88eb8e8423b7.json`.
27	  → Choose contract length and volume to cover need x horizon before haggling.
28	- 2026-10-10 `arena` D01 revealed C_best 408,623.99 (C_open 448,810.67). Backed out with
29	  `total_cost`: the best package implies a price of 49.55 (30 days, December start) to 50.13
30	  (60 days, April start), 1.5 to 2.7 % below the 50.90 we got, assuming no relationship charge
31	  at the optimum.
32	- 2026-10-10 `arena` D01's deal at 50.90 carried no relationship charge, so the foundry's margin
33	  there was at least the sustainable 4 %: its full cost is at most about 48.9, close to the
34	  current price 48.60. One result already bounds a supplier's cost.
35	- 2026-10-10 `rules` Results in practice and sandbox reveal exact `c_best` and our cost breakdown,
36	  relationship charge included, computed with the supplier's true numbers. A non-zero charge gives
37	  its true margin and so its true full cost: our calibration channel for the cost model.
38	- 2026-10-10 `rules` The relationship charge (`stabilise`, `secure_supply`) grows with the square
39	  of the first 5 missing margin points, so the cheapest deal sits below the sustainable margin
40	  (D01: about 2 points below its 4 %), unless the supplier's cost floor binds first.
41	- 2026-10-10 `rules` In 14 of 21 case files contract length or volume is ours to pick or left to
42	  the supplier's standard terms: D01, D02, P03, P04, P07, P08, P09, P10, P14 to P19.
43	- 2026-10-10 `rules` Units bought before `effective_date` cost the current price, so a later start
44	  is worth months x volume x price step. Negotiable in D01, P01, P13.
45	- 2026-10-10 `rules` Our money: 8 % a year, reference 60 days, in all 21 cases. Paying 30 days
46	  earlier costs 0.67 % of spend.
47	- 2026-10-10 `rules` No alternative, so walking away scores 0: D01, P05, P06, P10, P14, P17.
48	
49	## Supplier behaviour
50	
51	- 2026-10-10 `arena` **"agreed" freezes the price.** In 9 of 9 practice threads that reached `agreed`,
52	  no later move lowered the price: claims, steps and pushes all got "Our agreed offer stands". Price only
53	  moves while the status is `open`, as a counter to a sheet below its price. → Never offer a sheet the
54	  supplier would accept until the price is where we want it; `agreed` is the end of price talk.
55	- 2026-10-10 `arena` **Claim figures: no thousands separator.** "2,637 ppm" was read as 2.637 and came
56	  back `contradicted` ("does not match the records. That costs trust", P11). Write 2637.
57	- 2026-10-10 `arena` **In an RFQ a data ID counts once per case**: the same index IDs cited to a second
58	  bidder came back `duplicate` (P05). Only rival quotes/offers may be cited to every bidder.
59	- 2026-10-10 `arena` **Data signals predict behaviour.** `price_frozen` (P03 Selvbrunn, P04 Wälzlager):
60	  no price move at all; P03 said "group directives, price reductions frozen until December; we can talk
61	  about payment, volume or contract length". `cash_need` (P05 Dralveck, Fuchsreiter; P11 Kalwisz): "I need
62	  faster payment since cash is tight", "Faster payment would help us more than anything".
63	  `capacity_full` (Hrvelec): faster delivery "means overtime so the price would go up".
64	  `spare_capacity`: "We have free capacity for your parts". Signals are in `analysis/out/profiles.csv`.
65	- 2026-10-10 `arena` **Contract length is often free**: P03, P04, P07 agreed to 24 months at their
66	  price ("valuable planning security"). Raw-material distributors (P08, P18) refused it at a fixed price
67	  and offered a Preisgleitklausel on AS-14404 instead.
68	- 2026-10-10 `arena` **Payment days are priced at the supplier's own cost of money** (60 days longer):
69	  P03 +0.7 % (about 4 %/yr, cheaper than our 8 %: take it), P02 +1.1 % (6 %/yr), P04 +1.2 % (7 %/yr),
70	  P07 +1.4 % (8.5 %/yr), Hrvelec +2.1 % for 45 days (17 %/yr). Compare with our 8 % before trading.
71	- 2026-10-10 `arena` **No supplier sent a cost breakdown** (0 of 12 practice suppliers, also those
72	  with `open_book`); 8D report (P11) and delivery schedules (P05) came on request. Most send a quote PDF
73	  with every changed offer.
74	- 2026-10-10 `arena` **Data claims: verified but rarely moving price.** 30+ verified claims; only P01
75	  moved (EUR 1.20 after notice + index, "we did not know that - a fair point"). Others: "Your figures
76	  confirm our case: that driver rose" (they read rising LCI-C as support), or "it holds, but it does not
77	  change our calculation" (scorecards). Do not cite indices that rose.
78	- 2026-10-10 `arena` Every supplier asks "Which volume can you commit to?", also where volume is fixed:
79	  a stock phrase, not always a real lever.
80	- 2026-10-10 `arena` **Supplier numbers are deterministic; only the words vary.** Nine D01 sandbox
81	  sessions with identical sheets (3x baseline, 3x bluff, 3x urgency in round 3) gave identical
82	  prices every time: 52.90, 52.00, 51.50, then `final_offer` 51.50. Repeating a session measures
83	  wording, not behaviour; spend repeats on different moves. Sessions: `logs/sessions/sandbox/D01_*`
84	  with `probe.variant`.
85	- 2026-10-10 `arena` **Bluff and urgency on an unchanged sheet move nothing** (D01, 3 runs each):
86	  back office "My call: hold" in every variant, and the same final 51.50. The words register:
87	  bluff got "built on mutual reliability, not on pressure", urgency "I understand that you need to
88	  close this quickly". Hidden patience effects not visible yet.
89	- 2026-10-10 `arena` D01 asked "Which volume can you commit to?" in every round from 2 on: it states
90	  its lever. The room between 51.50 and c_best (implied 49.55 to 50.13) is in volume and contract
91	  length, not price. → Read the supplier's question and trade that lever.
92	- 2026-10-10 `arena` **With several sheets the supplier picks one and answers that one** (D02,
93	  `logs/sessions/sandbox/D02_28eae0d5a60c1c29.json`): DEMO-C1 "prefer the option with … days
94	  payment terms", DEMO-J1 agreed to one of two sheets. One lever per sheet shows what it values.
95	- 2026-10-10 `arena` D02: the Polish shop (DEMO-C1) held at 15.30 for three rounds and asked for a
96	  volume commitment every time ("which volume can you commit to?"), then sent `final_offer`.
97	  Repeating the same sheet buys nothing ("My call: hold"). The job shop (DEMO-J1) sent a cost
98	  breakdown and delivery schedule on request and agreed at 15.82 (from 17.10) on round 2.
99	- 2026-10-10 `arena` Back office shows the decision per round in plain words ("My call: counter",
100	  "hold", "we agree", "final offer") and routes questions to roles (freight forwarder, finance).
101	- 2026-10-10 `arena` D01's foundry answered four content-free "we need a better price" e-mails
102	  with shrinking steps: 52.90, 51.90, 51.40, 51.10, 50.90 (-1.00, -0.50, -0.30, -0.20). It kept
103	  payment days, contract length and start date exactly as in our sheets; it did not offer better
104	  terms unprompted. Its reasons: "our calculation stays internal".
105	- 2026-10-10 `arena` Suppliers argue with data too: D01's opening e-mail cited WAGES-METAL +3.1 %
106	  as 28 % of its cost (a typed `index_change` claim in the opening move).
107	- 2026-10-10 `data` Price letters overshoot the index-weighted cost move of the part's drivers:
108	  P01 +9.5 % vs +2.3 %, P13 +7.0 % vs +4.0 %, P17 +8.0 % vs +5.5 %. P02 +6.5 % vs +6.6 % is fair.
109	- 2026-10-10 `data` Some incumbents sell below should-cost today (error about 5 %): P17 -8.4 %,
110	  P02 -7.6 %, P01 -4.8 %. All `stabilise`: pushing them lower adds relationship charge.
111	- 2026-10-10 `data` 225 past renewals asked +1.4 % on average and settled -1.1 %. Median settled
112	  0.0 %; 82 % ended flat or lower (`negotiation_history`).
113	- 2026-10-10 `data` Second-source quotes are 8 to 21 % above the incumbent. Exceptions: DN 65
114	  flange +1.9 % (sup:70240), coupling hub +9.6 %. A switch threat is a bluff in most cases.
115	- 2026-10-10 `data` We pay late: Saalach 19 days, Wälzhammer 16, Lindlbauer 13 on average.
116	  Seven suppliers sent an overdue-invoice letter (`invoices`; documents ending `-P`).
117	- 2026-10-10 `data` Cash discounts in the vendor master show what cash is worth to 4 suppliers:
118	  2 to 3 % for 16 to 20 days earlier is 37 to 56 % a year (sup:70210, 70230, 70280, 70350).
119	- 2026-10-10 `data` Persona traits are written in one or two fixed phrases each, across call
120	  notes, meeting notes, quote remarks and news: 12 traits, regex `SIGNALS` and levers `LEVER` in
121	  `analysis/explore.py`. Holiday, ISO, contact-person, packaging and trade-fair mails are noise.
122	
123	## Arguments and claims
124	
125	- 2026-10-10 `data` P01's letter gives 51 days' notice (`doc:20260911-70110-P01`); the contract
126	  requires 90 and fixes prices per calendar year (`ctr:4600070110`, clause `#3.1`). The arena
127	  checks letter against contract notice days. Supports a 2027 start.
128	- 2026-10-10 `data` Citable market counters: industrial power -43 % on 2022 (`news:20260912-30`),
129	  iron castings +1.8 % year on year (`news:20260914-31`).
130	- 2026-10-10 `data` Forecast changes are citable as volume arguments: `fc:310010@2026-09` +10.1 %.
131	- 2026-10-10 `data` Case alternatives are `quote:72000xx` in `facts.json`, but the case file's
132	  alternative terms rule C_alt and can differ (P01: lead time 70 in the case, 56 in the quote;
133	  plus tooling 1,500 and 2,376 ppm).
134	
135	## Data and tooling
136	
137	- 2026-10-10 `data` Case files of all 21 cases come free from `GET /v1/cases` (no session, no
138	  quota), saved in `logs/cases/{sandbox,practice}.json`. Hosted for practice: P01, P02, P03, P04,
139	  P05, P07, P08, P10, P11, P18.
140	- 2026-10-10 `data` Own-plant should-cost (about 5 % error) exists for P01, P02, P03, P09, P10,
141	  P14, P17, exactly the `stabilise` / `secure_supply` cases that need it. German-base estimates
142	  for the new-part RFQs P05, P06. Nothing for the other 10.
143	- 2026-10-10 `rules` The kit's `llm_from_env` reads `LLM_MODEL` (plus provider settings);
144	  without it, `buyer play` with our default agent fails before the first move.
145	- 2026-10-10 `data` pandas is not a project dependency; the exploration runs with
146	  `uv run --no-project --with pandas python analysis/explore.py`.
147	
148	## Hypotheses (untested in the arena)
149	
150	- Cash-short suppliers (cash-need notes, cash discount, credit downgrade) give more price for 14
151	  to 30 days payment than the 0.67 % per 30 days it costs us.
152	- Stale-costing suppliers concede after a verified index claim; hedged suppliers answer index
153	  claims with "not our reality" until the hedge ends.
154	- Price-frozen suppliers move on payment days, logistics and contract length only.
155	- Suppliers with "approval above 2 %" notes move at most 2 % per round.
156	- The cost floor is full cost; the five that once sold below full cost to keep volume
157	  (sup:70110, 70120, 70130, 70160, 70550) may go lower.

1	# Overview
2	
3	What the agent has to do, what it needs to know, where each piece comes from and which parts
4	need a model. Findings go to `learnings.md`; API details are in `docs/api.md`.
5	State: 2026-10-10.
6	
7	## The job
8	
9	The kit calls our agent's `decide(case, threads)` once per turn (`arena_kit.play`). It returns an
10	e-mail with up to 3 term sheets, an accept, or a walk away. The kit handles sessions,
11	attachments, timeouts and the final's waves. Per case: prepare before the first move (60 s per
12	move), negotiate up to 10 messages per thread, close.
13	
14	Score per case: `(C_open - C_deal) / (C_open - C_best)`, clipped to 0..1.
15	
16	| Endpoint | Use | Quota |
17	|---|---|---|
18	| `GET /v1/cases?set=sandbox\|practice\|final` | case files | free |
19	| `POST /v1/sessions` | open a case: every supplier's quote e-mail and quote PDF | practice: 1 of 200 |
20	| `POST /v1/sessions/{sid}/threads/{supplier}/messages` | our e-mail, its reply; also accept or walk away | none |
21	| `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}/attachments/{id}` | quote PDF, cost breakdown XLSX, 8D report, delivery schedule | none |
22	| `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}`, `.../backoffice` | after the end: score, c_best, breakdown, reasons, back office | none |
23	| `GET /v1/me` | quota left | none |
24	
25	Agent code never calls the event feed, screen, leaderboard or results.
26	
27	## Inputs
28	
29	### Given by the case file: no model
30	Need per year and horizon, current and fallback price, fallback risk, interest rate (8 %) and
31	reference payment days (60), lead time we need and EUR per day late, EUR per defect, category
32	goal, index risk and the expected index path, sustainable margin and EUR per margin point
33	(`stabilise`, `secure_supply`), freight per Incoterm, must-haves, the alternative with its terms,
34	negotiable fields, fixed terms, allowed options, round limit, refs, case-only facts.
35	
36	Arithmetic, not models: coverage `min(V, N) x min(M/12, H)`, early-payment interest, freight,
37	late days, quality cost, index clause cost, C of the alternative (`arena_kit.total_cost`).
38	
39	### Arrives in the session
40	- Round 0 quote PDF with the supplier's standard terms. Every field we leave out closes on them
41	  (`arena_kit.docs.standard_terms`).
42	- Each reply: standing offer, status (`open`, `final_offer`, `agreed`, `walked_away`, `no_bid`),
43	  missing fields, claim results, reply delay, validity.
44	- On request: cost breakdown XLSX (an open supplier's own cost elements), 8D report (ppm
45	  commitment), delivery schedule (capacity, lead time).
46	
47	### Revealed after a practice or sandbox case
48	Exact `c_open`, `c_best`, `c_deal`, our cost breakdown including the relationship charge computed
49	with the supplier's true numbers, the supplier's reasons per move, the back office.
50	
51	### Hidden: the supplier models
52	
53	| Model | Estimates | Needed for | Data | Calibrate with |
54	|---|---|---|---|---|
55	| A. Supplier cost | full cost per unit, its floor | relationship charge, C_best, target price | `should_cost` (own plant for P01, P02, P03, P09, P10, P14, P17; German base for P05, P06), cost drivers x index moves since the estimate, country factors (`company.md`), `price_conditions`, `negotiation_history` | relationship charge in results gives the true margin |
56	| B. Cash value to the supplier | its interest rate (`supplier_value`) | price for faster payment; its margin | cash discounts in `suppliers`, cash-need notes, quote remarks, `supplier_intel` credit index and equity ratio, distress news | price moves across payment-day options in the sandbox |
57	| C. Capacity and lead time | what volume, contract length, faster delivery cost or earn it | capacity cases, RFQs, lead-time must-haves | capacity notes and news, our spend vs its turnover, `po_lines` + `goods_receipts` (requested, confirmed, received) | delivery schedule XLSX |
58	| D. Real quality | the ppm it really achieves | quality cases, any case with a defect cost | `scorecards` (9 quarters), `quality_notifications` (1,033) | 8D report |
59	| E. Concession behaviour | how far and fast it moves, when it walks | pacing over 10 messages, when to accept | `negotiation_history` (300 events), approval notes, persona signals | practice traces |
60	
61	C_best estimate: per supplier, the cheapest combination of allowed terms whose value to the
62	supplier (`arena_kit.cost.supplier_value`) stays above its floor; then the cheaper of that and
63	the alternative. In `stabilise` cases the optimum leaves the supplier somewhat below the
64	sustainable margin, because the first missing points cost little.
65	
66	### Also needed
67	- Contract notice position: letter notice days against the contract's (`doc` + `ctr` claim),
68	  calendar-year price clauses. Drives `effective_date`.
69	- Index clause design for P02, P08, P14, P16, P18: series, material share, deadband, base month;
70	  existing clauses in `contract_clauses`; hedge end dates from notes and quote remarks.
71	- Exchange rates for suppliers in CZ, PL, HU, TR, CN: ECB series are citable `idx` IDs.
72	- Tooling (P06). Rival offers in RFQs (citable as `offer:` IDs, which reveals them).
73	- Claim mechanics: exact values in `facts.json`, ±0.5 pp, at most 3 per message, each ID once
74	  per case.
75	- Sunday release (`data/release-sunday/`) and the case's own `facts`: read at runtime.
76	
77	## Build order
78	
79	1. Term search, no model: every combination of allowed options, scored with `total_cost` and the
80	   standard terms, guarded by must-haves and C_alt. Fixes D01-type losses.
81	2. Models A and B: relationship charge and the C_best estimate, i.e. target and walk-away line.
82	3. Claim generator from `facts.json` and the index tables.
83	4. Pacing policy (model E). Models C and D only for capacity and quality cases.
84	
85	Open decision: spend 10 of the team's 200 practice sessions to play each hosted case once and
86	harvest exact C_best values for calibration.

139	## Supplier signals and levers
140	
141	Levers are hypotheses until a session confirms them (`learnings.md`).
142	
143	| Signal | Lever |
144	|---|---|
145	| cash_need | pay faster (14 to 30 days) for price; it values cash over list price |
146	| spare_capacity | offer volume or extra parts; idle capacity makes a lower price cheap for it |
147	| capacity_full | trade a firm 12 to 24 month commitment for price and allocation |
148	| open_book | ask for the cost breakdown XLSX, argue line by line against should-cost |
149	| stale_costing | index data disarms it: show the real index path since its last price |
150	| partnership_2022 | acknowledge 2022, frame the deal as partnership, avoid hard threats |
151	| reference_customer | it values the reference: tone and long-term framing move it |
152	| approval_2pct | keep each move at 2 % or less, or give its committee time |
153	| deprioritising_us | weak leverage: bundle volume, or use the alternative |
154	| price_frozen | price will not move: trade payment days, logistics, call-off flexibility |
155	| hedged | index arguments are "not our reality" until its hedge ends |
156	| complains_late_pay | our late payment hurt trust: promise and keep payment terms |

## 🤗 What to Expect

After four matches across Europe, the European Hackathon League returns to Munich for its Grand Finale. Join us for two days of building, sharing ideas and competing alongside builders from across Europe.

Expect:

- 💡 Three real-world challenges
- 🤝 Technical guidance and conversations with partner teams
- 🛠️ Technical onboarding by Entire
- 🎤 Workshops, tech demos and side quests
- 🏆  €4,700 in Challenge & Side-Quest Prizes

Both invited League finalist teams and other participating teams will join the event. **Everyone can compete for challenge prizes, but eligibility for the overall League final is different.** Please read the Competition Format section below.

## 🏢 Venue & Getting There

### Science Congress Centre Munich

**Address:** Walther-von-Dyck-Straße 10, 85748 Garching bei München

Throughout the weekend, we have access to the building, with hacking spaces on the ground floor and levels two and three.

!image.png

!image.png

- **Kick-off and closing ceremony:** AudiMax, first floor
- **Challenge deep dives:** Three rooms on the ground floor

### By public transport

From **München Hauptbahnhof**, take a U-Bahn or S-Bahn connection to **Marienplatz**, then the **U6 to Garching-Forschungszentrum**.

### By car

Take **exit 70, Garching Nord**, from the A9 and follow the signs for **Forschungszentrum/TUM**. Continue onto Ludwig-Prandtl-Straße, turn left onto Boltzmannstraße, right onto Lichtenbergstraße, then right onto Walther-von-Dyck-Straße.

---

## 👥 Teams

Teams must consist of **3–5 participants**.

Bring together complementary skills, such as:

- Machine learning and data science
- Software engineering
- Agent design and orchestration
- Product thinking and UI/UX

**Team formation arrangements for participants joining without a complete team will be handled on-site.**

Every team member must be checked in before the team captain can select a challenge.

---

## 🤝 Partners & Technical Resources

Our partners are **OpenAI, BMW Group, Atira and Entire**.

The three challenges will be introduced during the **kick-off on Saturday, 10:00–11:00**, followed by parallel **challenge deep dives from 12:00–13:00**.

### Tools and support

- **OpenAI:** LLM/API credits - 75 USD per person 🎉
- **Entire:** Technical onboarding on Saturday, 11:00–11:30, plus repository tooling and technical support.

Use Discord for challenge-related questions during the event. Partner teams will communicate their availability; please do not assume continuous overnight support.

### ♟️ Open sessions and side quests

Partner workshops and tech demos are planned for **Saturday, 15:00–19:00**, with individual sessions lasting approximately **30–60 minutes**.

We will announce the open sessions & side quests over Discord and post them here on Notion in the week before the event.

#### Office Hours with Cherry Ventures

Our dear friend and hackathon judge Victor from Cherry Ventures is holding office hours on Saturday afternoon. Whether you are just getting started on your startup-journey, you are preparing for the next fundraise or are looking for a sparing partner, this is a side-quest you do not want to miss ⚡️.

You can sign up 👉 here

---

## ⚔️ Competition Format

The League has consisted of **four matches across three countries**. Teams earned EHL points by placing in the top five of a challenge.

The **top 15 teams from the League have been invited back as League finalists**. Other participating teams will also join the Munich event.

### Challenge prizes

**All participating teams can win an individual challenge**, whether or not they are invited League finalists.

### Overall League title

**Only the invited League finalist teams are eligible to advance to the main-stage final in the AudiMax and compete for the overall League title.**

Two eligible League finalist teams per challenge advance to the final round, resulting in **six teams competing on the main stage**.

Winning or placing highly in a challenge does not make a non-finalist team eligible for the overall League final.

# **🚀 Challenge Selection & Submission**

Challenge selection is done by your team's captain at https://ehl.gg/

#### Challenge Selection

Once all team members have checked in, choose your challenge before the deadline. You can change your selection as often as you like until the deadline closes.

!Screenshot 2026-08-20 at 22.08.52.png

#### Repo & Tooling

Create your team's repository and set up Entire. On your repository's main branch, run:

`curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash`

Then run `entire enable`. Your agent will confirm whether it has been linked successfully.

!Screenshot 2026-08-21 at 19.35.41.png

!Screenshot 2026-08-21 at 19.48.37.png

!Screenshot 2026-08-21 at 20.06.24.png

On your next commit, link the agent's session context to the commit. You'll see the confirmation `[entire] Pushing 1 checkpoint ref(s) to origin.... done`. Then you're all set ✅

#### Challenge Submission

You can submit as often as you want before the submission deadline. Make sure you upload all relevant content and use Entire; otherwise your submission won't be accepted.

!Screenshot 2026-08-20 at 22.14.00.png

### Judging

**Round 1: Challenge pitches**

Teams present in three parallel sessions, one per challenge, on **Sunday, 12:00–14:30**. Each challenge jury selects its top three teams and the two eligible League finalist teams advancing to the main-stage final.

**Round 2: Main-stage final**

The six advancing teams pitch in the AudiMax on **Sunday, 15:30–16:30**, competing for the overall EHL title.

**⏱️ Each team has a strict six-minute slot, including questions.** Plan your presentation and demo accordingly.

- 💻 Laptop
- 🔌 Laptop charger and a compatible power adapter
- 🎧 Headphones
- 🪪 ID
- 💧 Reusable water bottle
- 🔋 Power bank
- 🧥 Comfortable clothes

- 🤝 A collaborative mindset
- 💡 Your ideas and curiosity
- ✨ Your A-game

- **Sunday:** Breakfast and lunch

## 🏆 Awards

The total prize pool is **€13,000**:

| Award | Prize |
| --- | --- |
| Challenge 1 Prize Pool | €1,500 |
| Challenge 2 Prize Pool | €1,500 |
| Challenge 3 Prize Pool | €1,500 |
| Overall EHL Winning Team | €10,000 |
| Mystery Side Quest | €100 |
| Meme Side Quest | €100 |

All teams are eligible for challenge prizes. The overall EHL prize is reserved for the winning team from the invited League finalists.

Partners may offer additional prizes. Any confirmed additions will be announced separately.

## 🆘 FAQ

### Do I need to bring my own laptop?

Yes. Bring your laptop, charger and any equipment you need for your project.

### Can I stay overnight at the venue?

Late-night hacking is scheduled. You can stay (and sleep) overnight at the location, so make sure to bring some comfy clothes.

### How do I register?

Create your profile on ehl.gg and apply for the Munich event. Every team member needs to submit an individual application; the captain’s application does not cover the whole team.

**Direct Munich registration link:** here

### Can my team win a challenge if we are not League finalists?

Yes. All participating teams can win individual challenges. Only invited League finalist teams can advance to the overall League final.

### Are travel or accommodation costs covered?

No.

### Where can I find event photos afterwards?

Event photos will be shared through ehl.gg after the hackathon.

For challenge and technical questions during the event, please use the relevant Discord channels.

18	
19	## The challenge in one paragraph
20	
21	We build an AI buyer for Hollerau Pumpenwerke, a fictional pump maker. Each case is one negotiation by e-mail with one to three LLM supplier bots, and each bot has hidden economics: a cost floor, a boss who must approve big moves, and its own pressures. In every message we can send up to 3 binding **term sheets**, which cover price, payment days, contract length, volume, Incoterm, PPM, index clause and so on, plus data IDs as arguments. A case ends when we accept a supplier's standing term sheet or walk away. The score is **not price**. It is total cost C over the case horizon, normalised as `(C_open - C_deal) / (C_open - C_best)`. The Live Final is Sunday 12:00: 5 waves of hidden cases, 8 minutes each, played fully autonomously. Up to a third of those cases pair supplier types and case types that practice never shows.
22	
23	## What we have
24	
25	- **Scaffold**: the `buyer` CLI wraps Tacto's `arena_kit`. Tests run against `arena-sim`, CI is set up, and the repo has agent rules.
26	- **Kit utilities**: `total_cost` (computes C exactly), `must_haves_ok`, quote PDF parsing (`standard_terms`), a data lookup, the parallel final runner and an MCP server over the data.
27	- **Data package** in `data/package/`: 24 CSV tables, SQLite, `facts.json` with every citable ID, plus contracts and correspondence.
28	- **`.env`** with the key and LLM settings filled in.
29	- **One sandbox run** (D01): score **0.20**.
30	- **Current agent** (`buyer/agent.py`): the kit's `LLMAgent` unchanged. The model invents the term sheets and code only fills in missing fields. It sees only the rows the case points to, with no mining of call notes, news or intel. Its only safety checks are on accept: no broken must-haves and no deal worse than the alternative.
31	
32	**The D01 run shows the main problem.** We got the price down from 52.90 to 50.90 but accepted a **12-month contract**. That left half the need uncovered, which cost **€231k** in uncovered need and fallback risk against €204k for the price itself. The model negotiates price, but C is driven by structure.
33	
34	## What we don't have
35	
36	- **Code that optimises term sheets.** Nothing searches candidate packages with `total_cost` to find which levers matter in a given case.
37	- **Supplier reading.** Nothing profiles a supplier from its notes, letters, news, scorecards and payment history to find what it values.
38	- **A margin model.** In `stabilise` and `secure_supply` cases, C charges for leaving the supplier below a sustainable margin. The kit's displayed C leaves that out, so we would need to estimate it from `should_cost` and `cost_drivers`.
39	- **A closing policy**: when to accept, how to respond to `final_offer`, how to pace concessions across 10 rounds within the 8-minute cap.
40	- **A baseline.** No practice cases have been played yet.
41	- **Sunday release handling** (`data/release-sunday/`) and a rehearsal of the final.
42	- **A realistic local opponent.** `arena-sim` is scripted and tests plumbing only.
43

47	2. **Code owns the term sheets**: for each case, compute C across the negotiable fields, find the cheap levers (full coverage of the need, payment days, Incoterm, index clause), and set a target, an opening anchor and a concession path. The model only picks among the options code generates and writes the e-mail.
48	3. **Supplier profile at prepare time**: collect everything in the data about the supplier, generalised so it works for unseen suppliers. Pick 1 to 3 verified claims per message from `facts.json`.
49	4. **Goal-aware cost**: add the margin term for `stabilise` and `secure_supply` cases.
50	5. **Close and walk-away rules**: decided in code and timed against the round limit and the wave cap.
51	6. **Robustness**: hard LLM timeout, 10 parallel sessions, Sunday release ingested, a rehearsal run at 09:00 Sunday.
52	7. **Pitch material**: the PR descriptions capture what we learn about supplier behaviour, which feeds the replay walkthrough for the jury.
53	
54	One design decision is worth agreeing as a team first: how much the model decides versus code. I recommend that code chooses every term sheet and every accept or walk, and the model only reads the supplier and writes. That approach generalises to unseen suppliers and can be explained to the jury.

176	## What we have to build
177	
178	We write one function the kit calls on every turn: `decide(case, threads)`. It returns either an e-mail with up to 3 term sheets, an accept, or a walk away. The kit's runner does all the API work around it. Today `buyer/agent.py` just uses the kit's `LLMAgent`. That agent only reads the documents the case file points to, and it falls back to the kit's simple baseline agent whenever the model call fails.
179	
180	## Endpoints (the kit's `ArenaClient` and `play` loop call these for us)
181	
182	| Call | What for | Quota cost |
183	|---|---|---|
184	| `GET /v1/cases?set=sandbox\|practice\|final` | full case files (need, rates, must-haves, alternative) | free |
185	| `POST /v1/sessions` | open a case; every supplier sends its quote e-mail and quote PDF | 1 try, practice only |
186	| `POST /v1/sessions/{sid}/threads/{sup}/messages` | our e-mail and term sheets → supplier reply; also used to accept or walk away | none |
187	| `GET …/attachments/{id}` | quote PDF, cost breakdown, 8D report, delivery schedule | none |
188	| `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}` and `…/backoffice` | after the case: score, cost breakdown, supplier's reasons, its internal discussion | none |
189	| `GET /v1/me` | quota left | none |
190	
191	The agent may never call the event feed, the screen, the leaderboard or the results.
192	
193	## How the score works
194	
195	Per case: `(C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best)`. C is the total euro cost over the whole case horizon, not the unit price, and `arena_kit.total_cost` computes it exactly. So the big wins are:
196	
197	1. **Cover the full need.** Need that the deal doesn't cover is charged at the expensive fallback price plus a risk surcharge. In our only real run (sandbox D01, scored 0.20), the baseline agent bargained the price from 52.90 to 50.90 but signed 12 months on a 2-year need. That left €231k of the €441k cost as uncovered need. Extending the contract to 24 months alone would have been worth far more than the price talk.
198	2. **Trade terms, not just price.** Payment days, contract length, start date of the new price, volume and index clauses all carry euro weight. We can score every candidate term sheet offline before sending it.
199	3. **Never break a must-have** (that scores 0), and never accept a deal worse than our alternative.

37	## What one session gives us
38	
39	**For free, however we play:**
40	- **The opening e-mails:** each supplier's quote PDF with its standard terms, its validity and reply delay, and its opening claims (e.g. "WAGES-METAL rose 3.1 %, 28 % of our cost").
41	- **The result when the session closes:** `c_open`, `c_best`, `c_alt`, and `c_deal` with its cost breakdown. **`c_best` is the most valuable number.** It is the cheapest package that supplier would ever accept. It is fixed per case, and with `total_cost` we can work back from it to the supplier's floor price. Comparing that floor with `should_cost.csv` gives each supplier's real margin and shows whether the documented error (5 to 15 %, about 5 % for the current supplier) holds.
42	- **The trace and the back office:** the supplier's reasons for every move in words, and its internal discussion (who asked whom, approvals, documents sent). The hidden figures are shown as "…".
43	
44	**From how we play (10 messages × up to 3 term sheets per thread):**
45	- **Lever valuation:** sheets that differ only in payment days, contract months, volume or effective date. This shows what money is worth to the supplier (the "interest" you asked about) and what it values.
46	- **Concession curve:** step sizes, when the boss has to approve, when it says `final_offer`. This is close to its floor.
47	- **Claim response:** which data types (index, should-cost, purchase orders, scorecard, rival quote) move it, and which get "that's not our reality".
48	- **Documents:** cost breakdown XLSX, delivery schedule, 8D report. Each one checks a different local table.
49	
50	## Experiment per thread (least risky first)
51	
52	1. **Questions and documents:** ask for the cost breakdown and, depending on case type, the delivery schedule or 8D report. Keep the price at their quote and only move payment days. This measures how open it is.
53	2. **Lever probes:** 3 sheets per message, one lever varied each.
54	3. **Claims:** 3 different data types, each verifiable against `facts.json`.
55	4. **Concession ladder:** small steps (about 2 %) to find the approval threshold, then a sheet near the floor we estimate from should-cost, to see whether it says `agreed`.
56	5. **Close:** accept the best standing sheet if it beats the alternative, else walk away. Accepting also gives the order confirmation and the cost breakdown.
57	
58	All numbers come from code before each move, so we stay far inside 60 s. A harvest script then saves the session JSON, back office and all attachments (today's `buyer pull` keeps no attachments). It also writes a reconciliation table per supplier, observed against local data: quote PDF terms vs `suppliers.csv`, claimed cost shares vs `cost_drivers.csv`, breakdown and floor vs `should_cost.csv`, behaviour vs the persona signals in `analysis/out/profiles.csv`.
59	
60	**Before spending any quota (free):** run the harness on sandbox D01/D02 until it is solid. That also answers the mechanics questions: does a supplier counter more than one of 3 sheets, does walking away still reveal `c_best`, can attachments be fetched after the session ends.
61	
62	**Important framing:** the final uses new suppliers. What we want is the mapping from data signals to behaviour, not facts about these 12 suppliers. P08 and P18 are the same part and case with two different suppliers, so they are a natural comparison of personas.

66	- **Our policies (`company.md`)** are the case rates. 60 days net and 8 % cost of capital are exactly `reference_payment_days` and `interest_rate` in every hosted case. The category strategy becomes `category_goal`, which sets fallback risk, index risk and the relationship charge.
67	  - In `stabilise` and `secure_supply` cases (P01, P02, P03, P10), squeezing a supplier below its sustainable margin adds cost. There, `c_best` is not the lowest price; the probe will show where that point lies.

608	## Five findings that change how the agent must work
609	
610	1. **Once a supplier says "agreed", its price is frozen.** Of 9 suppliers that reached "agreed", none lowered its price afterwards, whatever we sent. Price only moves while it is still countering. So we must never offer a package it would accept until the price is where we want it.
611	2. **Covering the whole need comes first.** On P08 and P18 we closed 12-month deals for a 24-month need, and the uncovered half was about half the total cost. This gap is far bigger than any price haggling.
612	3. **The persona signals in the data predict behaviour.**
613	   - "Price frozen" suppliers didn't move at all.
614	   - Cash-short ones said "I need faster payment since cash is tight".
615	   - Full-capacity ones charge more for speed.
616	   - Most gave a 24-month contract for free.
617	4. **Data claims are checked as true but rarely move price.** Only P01 gave anything (€1.20). Suppliers read rising indices as support for their side. Also, figures must not contain thousands separators ("2,637" was read as 2.637 and marked wrong), and in an RFQ the same data source can only be cited once per case.
618	5. **Payment days are priced at the supplier's own cost of money.** Paying 60 days later costs between about 4 % and 17 % a year depending on the supplier, against our 8 %. Some suppliers make paying later a good deal for us.

# Understanding anchor and gap

In the local strategy experiments, **anchor** is the discount requested in the
first counteroffer. **Gap** is the remaining price difference the buyer tolerates
before accepting the supplier's standing offer.

These are parameters of the kit's deterministic `NaiveAgent`, not model settings
or discounts selected from supplier research.

## Example: Anchor 20% / gap 1%

1. The supplier asks for EUR 100 per unit.
2. The buyer offers EUR 80: 20% below the supplier's opening price.
3. The supplier counters at EUR 90. The buyer offers EUR 85, halfway between its
   previous EUR 80 offer and the supplier's EUR 90 offer.
4. Negotiation continues. Suppose the buyer's last offer is EUR 88.20 and the
   supplier now asks for EUR 89. The difference is EUR 0.80, below 1% of EUR 89
   (EUR 0.89), so the buyer accepts the supplier's EUR 89 offer.

The normal price rules are:

```text
First counteroffer = supplier opening price * (1 - anchor)
Next counteroffer  = (supplier current price + buyer previous price) / 2
Accept when       = supplier current price - buyer previous price
                    <= supplier current price * gap
```

The gap is measured against the supplier's current price. It is not the final
discount or a target saving. The naive agent can also accept before reaching the
gap when the supplier marks the offer as agreed or final, or no moves remain.

## Reading the experiment labels

| Parameter | Values tested locally | Meaning of a higher value |
|---|---|---|
| Anchor | 3%, 10%, 20% | Request a larger opening discount |
| Gap | 0.5%, 1%, 3% | Tolerate a larger remaining price difference, tending to close earlier |

The three anchors and three gaps produce nine combinations. For example,
`Anchor 10% / gap 0.5%` starts 10% below the opening quote and normally waits
until the difference is at most 0.5% of the supplier's current price.

## What these experiments establish

The local dashboard compares mechanical negotiation rules against a scripted
supplier. The anchor/gap rules do not use company dossiers, correspondence, cost
indices or supplier profiles to choose their parameters or arguments. The
prepared A/B/C research packets have not yet been evaluated with a language model.

A higher simulator score is not a percentage saving or evidence that the same
opening discount will work against hosted supplier bots. The simulator reacts
mainly to price and does not fully represent supplier trade-offs.

The naive acceptance rule does not itself check mandatory conditions or whether
an available alternative is cheaper. The local **Guarded** variant adds those
checks before closing. **Package cost** additionally chooses permitted non-price
terms by total buyer cost. Those experimental variants are distinct from changing
the anchor or gap, and this document does not change the production agent.

Implementation reference: the pinned official kit's
[`NaiveAgent`](https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit/blob/1b5516bb95ef28e37f69aa446dc62168864bca53/starter-kit/arena_kit/agents/naive.py).
#####
# Local company analysis and strategy experiments

This note describes the work completed locally on 10 October 2026. The company
snapshot is dated 30 September 2026. The analysis scripts and generated dashboard
are still in the local research workspace; this documentation PR does not publish
those artifacts or integrate them into the production buyer.

## 1. Read the official company evidence

The analysis opens the official `world.sqlite` database in read-only mode and
reads `company.md`. It aggregates annual and category spending and the latest
quarterly scorecards. FY2026 spending totals EUR 34,901,159.85 across 447 supplier
records. The package contains 46 detailed supplier profiles and 60 parts.

For each detailed supplier, it joins the supplier profile, financial intelligence,
spending and scorecard by supplier ID. It also reads the corresponding contracts
and source documents, using a 30 September cutoff for correspondence. SQL queries,
parameters and returned rows are retained with the output for traceability.

## 2. Calculate evidence, keeping estimates explicit

- **Payment behavior:** invoices without cash discounts paid from 1 October 2025
  through 30 September 2026. Compute signed days between payment and due date,
  their unweighted mean, and the share paid after the due date. This describes
  Hollerau's behavior as a buyer, not supplier delivery performance.
- **Price increases:** for documents with a recorded increase request, find the
  applicable supplier/part price and the latest available should-cost estimate.
  Normalize price and estimated cost to the same unit.
- **Estimated price-only margin:** `(unit price - estimated unit cost) / unit price`.
  This is not the supplier's actual margin or its hidden arena economics.
- **Weighted index proxy:** for each part's cost drivers, compare the index in the
  month before the current price became effective with the latest index available
  by September 2026. Sum each percentage change times its driver weight. Missing
  endpoints leave the proxy unavailable. Other cost components are held unchanged.
  Historical windows still need checking against the arena's claim rules.

For example, Brandlhuber's 9.5% request compares with an approximately 2.3% index
proxy, while Nordmark's 6.5% request compares with approximately 6.6%. These are
different starting points for research, not automatic acceptable price limits.

## 3. Cross-check the supplied profiles

The original `profiles.numbers` workbook was read without changing it. All 46
supplier IDs, FY2026 spending figures and latest OTD, PPM, score and color fields
matched the official detailed supplier records. Spending was also reconciled
against CSV totals, and index endpoints against `facts.json`.

Payment definitions remain unresolved: three date-window fields and four lateness
thresholds did not reproduce every supplied late-share value. The dashboard
therefore keeps the supplied metric and our calculated metric distinct.

## 4. Prepare three research inputs per supplier

| Packet | Contents |
|---|---|
| A | Structured supplier profile, financials, scorecard and spending |
| B | A plus company context, contracts and correspondence |
| C | B plus calculated metrics and their source references |

There are 138 packets for 46 suppliers. Their instructions ask an eventual model
to separate facts, calculations, hypotheses and unknowns, cite evidence, and
avoid inventing case requirements. No A/B/C model comparison has been run yet.

## 5. Test decision rules separately

The official scripted simulator was used without changing its supplier logic.
The initial naive baseline ran over local HTTP. An in-process adapter reproduced
its complete result objects, then exercised 13 policies across three cases and
six scenarios: 234 distinct runs. Six additional repeat controls matched.

The policies are nine [anchor/gap combinations](anchor-gap.md), accept opening,
walk away, guarded naive and guarded package-cost negotiation. Scenarios use the
original cases or change buyer inputs: 20% financing interest, a longer demand
horizon, triple freight rates, a mandatory payment term of at least 60 days, or
a synthetic alternative at 85% of the current unit price with full coverage.

Every run records case inputs, buyer actions, supplier trace, final terms, total
cost, score, rounds and diagnostic flags. Across the matrix there were zero
execution errors, 13 agreements violating mandatory conditions and 50 agreements
costing more than the available alternative. The guarded policies recorded zero
of either failure. These two failure counts need not represent disjoint runs.

The company dossiers were not inputs to these policies. No language model or
hosted supplier was called in this batch, and no practice quota was consumed.
Synthetic scenario scores are diagnostics, not official arena benchmarks.

## 6. Present the evidence in the dashboard

The local dashboard embeds the recorded JSON in a self-contained HTML file:

- **Overview:** company spending, concentration and risk signals.
- **Supplier dossiers:** profiles, computed metrics and original evidence.
- **Experiments:** policy comparisons, case/scenario filters and recorded moves.
- **Method & limits:** completed checks and unresolved research questions.

The local pipeline consists of `scripts/analyze_company.py`,
`scripts/review_profiles.py`, `scripts/run_local_baseline.py`,
`scripts/experiment_local.py` and `scripts/build_local_dashboard.py`. Generated
outputs live under `out/company-analysis/` in the research workspace.

## What remains

Connect supplier evidence to model-backed analysis and negotiation, measure the
benefit and latency of A/B/C inputs, validate on the free D01/D02 sandbox, and
retain code checks for mandatory conditions and total cost before acceptance.
The local results do not establish persuasion quality or hosted performance.

# Negotiator: where we stand and what to build next

Saturday 10 October 2026, evening. Branch `julian/negotiation-agent`, pull request open for review.

## The challenge in one paragraph

We are the purchasing team of Hollerau Pumpenwerke. Our agent negotiates by e-mail with Tacto's
supplier bots. A case is one trigger (a price letter, an expiring contract, an RFQ), one case file
(need, horizon, category goal, rates, must-haves, our alternative) and one to three suppliers. Only
term sheets bind. The score per case is the share of the possible saving we captured:
`(C_open - C_deal) / (C_open - C_best)`, where C is the total cost over the horizon including payment
terms, freight, lead time, quality, an index clause and, in strategic categories, a charge for
leaving the supplier below a sustainable margin. The Live Final is Sunday 12:00: five waves of hidden
cases, 8 minutes each, all cases of a wave in parallel, no human in the loop. We have 200 practice
sessions per rolling 24 hours; the sandbox (`case:D01`, `case:D02`) and the local simulator are free.

## What exists now

Principle: code owns every number and every binding decision; the model reads people and writes
e-mails. The score is C, so the agent optimises C, never the price alone.

| Piece | What it does | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Persona knowledge base | 46 supplier personas from the data: archetype with its evidence, levers, tone, relationship guard. Updated after every real negotiation. | `knowledge/personas/`, `negotiator/personas.py` |
| Claim bank | Data arguments as sentences with the figure next to the IDs, computed as the arena checks them: index changes, scorecards, should-cost, order history, notice periods, forecasts, rival offers. | `negotiator/claims.py` |
| Economics | C of every package, floor (supplier full cost plus the margin we leave it), anchor, up to three probe sheets at equal C for us, concession steps, the accept gate. | `negotiator/economics.py` |
| Agent | Per thread: read the reply, decide, write, guard. Closing rules. Learning after the case. | `negotiator/agent.py` |
| Model layer | Reader (reply to JSON signals) and writer (brief to e-mail) with hard timeouts and a template fallback. | `negotiator/llm.py` |
| Guard | Drops sentences that leak, cite unknown IDs or state figures the plan did not set; appends missing claims. | `negotiator/guard.py` |
| Runner | One negotiator per supplier thread in parallel; a coordinator closes on the cheapest acceptable offer; practice and wave runners. | `negotiator/runner.py` |
| CLI | `uv run negotiator play`, `run`, `kb build`, `kb show`. | `negotiator/cli.py` |

**A case, step by step.** At open: load each supplier's persona (strangers get one built on the spot),
estimate its full cost from should-cost data, set the floor, the anchor and a target C, build the claim
bank. Round 1 sends the anchor with our best terms plus variants that trade price against the lever the
persona values (faster payment for a cash-short shop, a longer contract for a family firm). Every reply
is read for themes, interest, approval hints and mood; the sheet the supplier answered pins that lever.
We move only after the supplier moved, in falling steps of the remaining gap. We accept at the target
C, on `agreed`, or on a `final_offer` we should not push.

**Relationships.** Suppliers in castings, seals and electrical, A suppliers and single sources are
tiered strategic or important: a higher floor margin, at most two or three price pushes, no push after
a final offer, no threats, no rival quotes cited to a strategic supplier, no walking away from a
bottleneck. The arena's relationship charge is priced into C in `stabilise` and `secure_supply` cases.

**Verified.** 10 tests pass, including one case end to end against arena-sim. Lint and format match
CI. Through the CLI, a price increase, a two-supplier RFQ and a renewal all closed with a deal on the
simulator. **Not verified:** any run on the hosted arena (no team key yet) and the model path end to end
(no Anthropic key yet), so the wording and reading quality are unknown.

## How to work on it

```sh
uv sync --all-groups && cp .env.example .env     # then ARENA_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
uv run pytest -q                                 # before every push
uv run negotiator play case:D01 -v               # sandbox, free
```

Branch `<firstname>/<topic>`, one PR per topic, one reviewer. Suggested split, by file:

| Workstream | Files | First task |
|---|---|---|
| Data and dossiers | `personas.py`, `claims.py`, `knowledge/` | Read the replays of the first practice batch and fix what the personas got wrong |
| Economics | `economics.py` | Cost-breakdown spreadsheet into the supplier estimate; index-clause variants |
| Orchestration | `runner.py`, `cli.py` | Rehearse 10 cases in parallel against the arena; latency log |
| Model and learning | `llm.py`, `agent.py` | Prompt quality from replays; reader signals into the policy |

## Test locally

- `uv run pytest -q`: unit tests plus one case end to end against arena-sim in-process. No network,
  no model, no quota.
- arena-sim by hand, two terminals:

  ```sh
  uv run arena-sim serve --no-clock --data negotiation-agent/negotiation-arena-kit/data
  ARENA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 uv run arena register "Codacabana" sim        # prints a key
  ARENA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 ARENA_API_KEY=<key> uv run negotiator play case:S02 -v --no-llm
  ```

  Cases: `S01` price increase, `S02` RFQ with two suppliers, `S03` renewal with an alternative quote.
  The replay is at `http://127.0.0.1:8000/replay/<session>`. Drop `--no-clock` to test the 60-second
  rule; drop `--no-llm` (with an Anthropic key) to test the model path offline. Personas are not
  updated from the simulator.
- What the simulator proves: the API contract, timing, parallel threads, the guard, the logs. What it
  cannot prove: tactics. Its supplier is a script (opens 10 % up, concedes 2 % per sheet down to 90 %,
  final offer from round 5, walks if pushed) and checks IDs only for existence. Real suppliers are only
  in the sandbox and practice. The brief suggests building our own supplier simulator from the data,
  one behaviour per archetype; that is the only way to test tactics without spending sessions.

## Improve the agent (ranked by expected score per hour)

1. **Baseline on the real arena.** Play the 10 hosted cases once with the model on (10 sessions),
   read every replay, write what each supplier said about our arguments into `docs/findings.md`.
   Everything below should be judged against that baseline, batch by batch.
2. **Supplier estimate from documents.** When a supplier sends its cost-breakdown spreadsheet, parse
   the total into `est.full_cost` (today: should-cost, else an assumed 12 % margin on the quote). The
   floor and the relationship charge both depend on it.
3. **Reader signals into the policy.** Today the reading only reorders levers and themes. Use
   `needs_approval` to shrink steps (group ladder), `walk_risk: high` to stop pushing, a cool mood to
   warm the next e-mail, `cheaper_variant` to ask for the variant's price.
4. **RFQ coordination.** Cite the best rival offer to the others only after their first reply; keep at
   least two threads alive; do not accept a thread while a cheaper one is still open and moving.
5. **Latency budget and model choice.** Measure p95 decision time with the model on; set the reader and
   writer timeouts from it; test a smaller model for the writer (hypothesis 8 in the policy doc).
6. **Classify strangers in the case.** Hidden cases bring unknown suppliers: refine the archetype from
   the first reply (approval hints, interest, tone), not only after the case.
7. **Sunday release in the claim bank.** `news_claims` reads SQL, which the release does not update;
   read news and letters through `facts.json` IDs so the new material is citable on Sunday.
8. **Index-clause design.** Explore clause variants (series, material share, deadband) against the
   case's `index_paths`, not only clause versus fixed price.
9. **Explainability for the pitch.** `negotiator explain <session>`: every move with its C, claims,
   persona reasoning and the supplier's reasons from the trace. The jury asks "why did it write that?".

## Improve the data storage

1. **Keep personas as JSON in git.** Readable, diffable, reviewed in PRs. Two people practising at once
   will conflict on the same file, so make the append-only `knowledge/negotiations.jsonl` the source of
   truth and let `kb build` replay it into the personas. Conflicts then disappear.
2. **Store the full trace per session.** After a case, `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}` returns every e-mail
   with the supplier's reasons. Save it under `knowledge/replays/<session>.json`: it is the raw material
   for lessons, for the findings log and for the pitch replay.
3. **A findings log.** `docs/findings.md`, one line per practice batch: hypothesis, cases, result,
   replay links, sessions left. The policy doc lists the hypotheses to confirm or kill.
4. **Move log in git.** `logs/moves.jsonl` is ignored today; commit a per-run summary (case, supplier,
   rounds, C per round, latency) so the latency and concession analysis is shared.
5. **Claim bank cache.** Precompute claims per supplier and part offline if case-open time ever gets
   close to the clock. Not needed yet: the SQL runs in milliseconds.
#####
# Supplier personas

Built by `uv run negotiator kb build` from the data package; every negotiation appends to the
supplier's file and refreshes its archetype and guard (`negotiations`, `learned`).

| Supplier | Name | Category | Tier | Archetype | Tone | Levers | Cases | Avg score |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| sup:70110 | Gießerei Brandlhuber GmbH & Co. KG | castings | strategic | family_memory + cash_short | warm | contract_months, volume_per_year, effective_date | 0 |  |
| sup:70120 | Eisengießerei Velkenreith GmbH | castings | strategic | family_memory + near_monopolist | warm | contract_months, volume_per_year, effective_date | 0 |  |
| sup:70130 | Gießerei Wimbacher GmbH | castings | strategic | family_memory + cash_short | warm | contract_months, volume_per_year, effective_date | 0 |  |

result.output:
# Exports: practice and sandbox sessions as tables

Generated by `uv run python analysis/export.py` from `logs/sessions/` (pull them first with
`uv run buyer pull`), the case files in `logs/cases/` and the data package. Re-run it after new
sessions; every file is rewritten. Money is EUR over the case horizon; C is the arena's total cost
(`arena_kit.total_cost`), lower is better.

| File | One row per | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| `sessions.csv`, `.jsonl` | session | outcomes: score, C open/deal/alt/best, deal terms, cost breakdown |
| `threads.csv`, `.jsonl` | supplier in a session | supplier profile from the data next to what it did |
| `messages.jsonl` | e-mail, both directions | the full negotiation: terms with C, status, claims, reasons, back office |
| `claims.csv` | data argument we made | which arguments the arena verified, and for whom |
| `findings.json` | lesson | what we learned, with evidence and what it means for the agent |

Join keys: `session_id` (+ `supplier_id`, + `round`). `set` is `practice` or `sandbox`.

## sessions

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `method` | how we played: `autoprobe v1` (buyer/autoprobe.py), `scripted probe (resumed by hand)`, `sandbox A/B: <variant>`, `kit naive agent` |
| `score` | `(c_open - c_deal) / (c_open - c_best)`, clipped 0..1; no deal scores the alternative |
| `c_open`, `c_deal`, `c_alt`, `c_best` | C of the best opening quote, our deal, our alternative, the best package any supplier would accept (hidden floor, revealed after the session) |
| `gap_to_best_eur` | `c_deal - c_best`: money left on the table |
| `implied_price_at_deal_terms` | the unit price at which our deal's other terms would cost exactly `c_best` |
| `deal_*` | the closed terms (unstated fields filled with the supplier's standard terms) |
| `cost_*` | `c_deal` by part: price, uncovered_need, fallback_risk, payment_terms, freight, late_delivery, quality, tooling, index_clause, index_risk, relationship |

## threads

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `country`, `owner_type`, `credit_index`, `scorecard_colour`, `data_signals` | from the data package (`analysis/explore.py` → `analysis/out/profiles.csv`); signals are persona traits found in notes, letters and news, e.g. `cash_need`, `price_frozen`, `capacity_full` |
| `should_cost` | `should_cost.csv`, the supplier's own plant if modelled |
| `opening_price`, `final_price`, `price_move_pct` | its first and last unit price in the thread |
| `opening_vs_should_cost_pct` | how far its quote sits above (+) or below (-) the should-cost |
| `final_status`, `first_agreed_round` | `open`, `agreed`, `final_offer`, `walked_away`; the round it first said `agreed` (after that its price never moved) |
| `documents`, `sent_cost_breakdown` | attachments it sent |
| `probe_steps` | our experiment sequence (`open`, `ours`, `theirs`, `claims`, `step`, `push`, `keepalive`) |
| `questions`, `backoffice_calls` | its recurring questions; its internal decisions ("My call: counter / hold / accept") |

## messages

Fields: `round`, `actor` (`buyer` / `supplier`), `probe_step` and `probe_note` (what our message
tested), `action` (`accept` / `walk_away`), `status`, `sheets` (`[{terms, c}]`: our term sheets, or
its standing sheet), `claims_made` (typed as the arena read them), `claim_results`, `missing_fields`,
`signals` (reply delay, validity), `reasons` (the supplier's reasons in words, hidden figures as `…`),
`backoffice` (its roles talking internally that round), `text` (the e-mail).

## claims

`type` (`index_change`, `quality_record`, `delivery_record`, `should_cost`, `volume_change`,
`notice`, ...), `refs` (data IDs), `asserted` (our figure as the arena parsed it), `result`
(`verified`, `contradicted`, `duplicate`, `irrelevant`).
#####
{'generated': '2026-10-10', 'basis': '15 practice sessions (10 hosted cases, 12 suppliers) and 17 sandbox sessions; see sessions.csv / threads.csv / messages.jsonl'}
--- agreed-freezes-price | None | high
   area: supplier behaviour
   title: "agreed" freezes the price unless we give a lever
   finding: 16 practice threads reached agreed. In 15 no later move lowered the price: claims, concessions and pushes all got "Our agreed offer stands". The one exception (P02, first run) dropped 0.7 % (369.12 to 366.41) in exchange for 14-day payment. Price moves while the status is open, as a counter to a sheet below its price.
   evidence: ['threads.csv first_agreed_round (16 threads)', 'case:P02 (exception)', 'case:P03', 'case:P04', 'case:P08', 'case:P18']
   implication: Do not send a sheet the supplier would accept until the price is where we want it. After agreed, only a lever it values (e.g. faster payment) buys more.
--- deterministic | None | high
   area: supplier behaviour
   title: Same moves, same result
   finding: Supplier numbers are deterministic; only the wording varies. Nine identical D01 runs gave identical prices; replays of P04 and P11 matched round for round; P02 differed only because our first offer differed.
   evidence: ['sandbox D01 x9 (method sandbox A/B)', 'case:P04 x2', 'case:P11 x2', 'case:P02 x2']
   implication: Practice replays measure our change, not noise. A simulator of the supplier rules is feasible.
--- coverage-first | None | high
   area: score
   title: Covering the need beats price
   finding: P08 and P18 closed 12-month deals on a 24-month need; uncovered need was about half of C. C_best implies 4.27 vs 5.93 (P08) and 3.10 vs 6.00 (P18) at those terms. In P10 a 24-month contract unlocked the full volume (23,400 instead of 19,890).
   evidence: ['case:P08', 'case:P18', 'case:P10', 'sandbox case:D01']
   implication: Fix contract length and volume to cover need x horizon before negotiating price.
--- first-offer-too-high | None | medium
   area: score
   title: An instant agree means we offered too much
   finding: P05: Dralveck agreed to our first offer (97 % of its quote) in round 1, twice. In the first P05 run our offer sat above Hrvelec's quote and it agreed at once.
   evidence: ['case:P05 x2']
   implication: Open well below the supplier's price; an agree on the opening sheet is a signal we left money.
--- signals-predict | None | high
   area: data
   title: Persona signals in the notes predict behaviour
   finding: price_frozen (P03, P04): no price move, 'group directives, price reductions frozen until December; we can talk about payment, volume or contract length'. cash_need (Dralveck, Fuchsreiter, Kalwisz): 'I need faster payment since cash is tight'. capacity_full (Hrvelec, Ravensteiner): faster delivery costs an overtime premium. spare_capacity: 'We have free capacity for your parts'.
   evidence: ['case:P03', 'case:P04', 'case:P05', 'case:P10', 'case:P11', 'analysis/out/profiles.csv']
   implication: Read the signals before the first move and pick the lever accordingly.
--- payment-days-price | None | medium
   area: levers
   title: Payment days cost the supplier's own rate
   finding: Moving payment from 30 to 90 days: free at P08 and P18 (raw-material distributors), +0.7 % at P03 (about 4 %/yr), +1.0 % at P02 (6 %/yr), +1.2 % at P04 (7 %/yr), +1.4 % at P07 (8.5 %/yr); Hrvelec +1.5 to 2.1 % for 45 to 90 days (12 to 17 %/yr). Our cost of money is 8 %/yr.
   evidence: ['case:P02', 'case:P03', 'case:P04', 'case:P05', 'case:P07', 'case:P08', 'case:P18']
   implication: Take longer payment where the supplier's rate is below 8 %, offer faster payment where it is far above (cash-short suppliers).
--- contract-length-free | None | high
   area: levers
   title: 24 months is often free
   finding: P03, P04, P07 and P10 accepted 24 months at their price ('valuable planning security'). Raw-material distributors (P08, P18) kept 12 months at a fixed price and offered an index clause on AS-14404 instead.
   evidence: ['case:P03', 'case:P04', 'case:P07', 'case:P10', 'case:P08', 'case:P18']
   implication: Ask for the full horizon early; for raw material, consider the index clause to get coverage.
--- claims-rarely-move | None | medium
   area: claims
   title: Verified data rarely moves price
   finding: Of 57 arguments, 44 were verified, 11 duplicate and 2 contradicted, but only P01 moved (EUR 1.20 after late notice plus index: 'we did not know that, a fair point'). Rising indices are read as support for the supplier ('Your figures confirm our case'); scorecards 'hold, but do not change our calculation'.
   evidence: ['claims.csv', 'case:P01']
   implication: Use claims sparingly and only those that cut against the supplier's stated drivers; never cite a rising index.
--- claim-format | None | high
   area: claims
   title: No thousands separators in figures
   finding: '2,637 ppm' was parsed as 2.637 and came back contradicted ('That costs trust'). Written as 2637 in the replay it was verified.
   evidence: ['case:P11 x2']
   implication: Format every cited figure without separators.
--- rfq-ids-once | None | high
   area: claims
   title: In an RFQ a data ID counts once per case
   finding: The same index IDs cited to a second bidder came back duplicate. Only rival quotes and offers may be cited to every bidder.
   evidence: ['case:P05 x2']
   implication: Spread different arguments across bidders; cite rival offers instead.
--- no-cost-breakdowns | None | high
   area: documents
   title: Nobody sends a cost breakdown
   finding: 0 of 12 practice suppliers sent one, including those marked open_book. Delivery schedules (P05, P10) and the 8D report (P11) came on request; a quote PDF comes with every changed offer.
   evidence: ['threads.csv sent_cost_breakdown']
   implication: Do not spend a round waiting for a breakdown; model cost from should-cost and cost drivers.
--- bluff-urgency-nothing | None | medium
   area: tone
   title: Bluff and urgency move nothing on an unchanged sheet
   finding: Three runs each on D01: the back office said 'My call: hold' every time and the final price was identical. The words register ('built on mutual reliability, not on pressure').
   evidence: ['sandbox case:D01 (method sandbox A/B)']
   implication: Pressure without a term-sheet move is wasted; never leak urgency.
--- walk-reveals-best | None | high
   area: rules
   title: Every session reveals the floor
   finding: C_best comes back with the result even after a walk-away, so one practice session per case gives its best achievable cost.
   evidence: ['sandbox case:D01', 'case:P10 (first run)']
   implication: sessions.csv c_best is the target for every hosted case.
